intended_object: The cofree right C-comodule M ⊗_R C (coaction id ⊗ Δ followed by reassociation), viewed as an object of the full subcategory of finitely generated comodules when M ⊗_R C is finitely generated over R. This comes from the docstring and the module documentation (Sweedler, Ch. 2).
explanation: The definition bundles `M ⊗[R] C` with the `Comodule.cofree` structure as an object of `FGComoduleCat R C` (the full subcategory of comodules whose underlying module is finitely generated). It does this with `of`, using the local instance `Comodule.cofree`. The `Module.Finite R (M ⊗[R] C)` hypothesis is exactly what membership in that subcategory requires. The coaction is `(assoc)⁻¹ ∘ (id_M ⊗ Δ)`, sending m ⊗ c to ∑ (m ⊗ c₁) ⊗ c₂, which is the standard cofree comodule. The setting (commutative semiring, any coalgebra, any module M) is fully general. The theorem `incl_cofree` shows this is the ambient `ComoduleCat.cofree` restricted to the finite case, and `cofreeEquiv` gives the expected universal property. This Mathlib version has no comodule category or cofree comodule to compare with.
